mechanism_inventory: missing access control on reallocate (permissionless entry by any caller)
stale accounting snapshot / reward-index update ordering in ReallocationLogic (interest not settled before reallocation changes LP position)
wrong lifecycle ordering (reallocation executed when pair is in invalid/uninitialized state)
external-call failure / DoS via malicious settlementData callback (unhandled revert in settlement contract locks the pool)
precision / packing / normalization edge in LP token accounting after range shift
victim accounting direction: LP suppliers may lose unrealized fees or suffer unfavorable range after reallocation initiated by any third party
missing invariant enforcement: no check that reallocation is actually needed (out-of-range condition not enforced before mutating state)

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: reallocate() has no access-control guard — it is protected only by nonReentrant. Any EOA can call it at any time for any pairId. The actual accounting mutations (range shift, LP position close/reopen, fee settlement, index updates) are all delegated to ReallocationLogic.reallocate(). The caller supplies arbitrary settlementData bytes that are passed directly into the settlement callback, giving a permissionless actor control over a privileged settlement path.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged EOA, no role or allowance required. Calls reallocate(pairId, maliciousSettlementData).
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker calls PredyPool.reallocate(pairId, settlementData) — passes nonReentrant, no other gate. 2. Delegates to ReallocationLogic.reallocate(globalData, pairId, settlementData). 3. ReallocationLogic executes range reallocation including closing existing Uniswap V3 LP position and reopening at a new range. 4. During settlement callback (predySettlementCallback or equivalent), attacker-controlled settlementData routes execution through an attacker-supplied settlement contract. 5. Attacker can time the call to maximally disadvantage LP suppliers (e.g., when the new range is unfavorable, when fees are about to accrue, or when the price is at a boundary causing maximum slippage during range reallocation). 6. LP suppliers (bond token holders) suffer range-reallocation at an attacker-chosen time, potentially losing accumulated fees or receiving worse LP economics.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: LP suppliers / bond token holders who hold positions in the affected pair. They bear the economic cost of range reallocation (fee loss, slippage during position reopen) triggered at an adversarial time.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker may gain arbitrage profit by front-running or sandwiching the reallocation, or may simply grief LP suppliers. The settlement contract supplied by the attacker receives token flows during settlement.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Permissionless entry is confirmed by source — no modifier beyond nonReentrant. Attacker-supplied settlementData is passed through without validation in PredyPool. The economic damage to LP suppliers from adversarially-timed reallocation is a real, material impact distinct from a self-funded or dust-level outcome.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: settlementData is opaque bytes passed from an unprivileged caller directly into ReallocationLogic, which presumably invokes an ISettlement callback. The settlement contract address or routing is encoded in these bytes. There is no whitelist or validation of the settlement contract in PredyPool.reallocate(). A malicious settlement contract can revert selectively or perform unexpected token movements during the callback.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged EOA encoding a malicious ISettlement address in settlementData.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker calls reallocate(pairId, encodedMaliciousSettlementData). 2. ReallocationLogic calls into the attacker's settlement contract during the settlement phase. 3. Malicious contract reverts conditionally (e.g., only when called in a state that is bad for the pool) causing the reallocation to fail and leaving the LP position partially closed or in an inconsistent intermediate state. 4. The nonReentrant guard prevents re-entry into PredyPool itself, but does not prevent the settlement contract from interacting with other protocols or returning manipulated data.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: LP suppliers and the protocol — if settlement fails mid-reallocation, the LP position may be left partially unwound, causing solvency risk.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker can grief the protocol or selectively cause DoS on reallocation for a target pair.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Source confirms settlementData is passed unvalidated from an arbitrary external caller. The ISettlement import is present. Impact (DoS on reallocation / partial state corruption) clears at least Medium severity. This affects a different impact path (availability / partial state) than the LP-economics mechanism above.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: stale accounting snapshot / interest not settled before reallocation mutates LP position
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: reallocate() calls ReallocationLogic.reallocate() which must close and reopen Uniswap V3 LP positions. If accumulated interest or fee indices are not flushed before the LP position is changed, the per-share accounting for bond token holders will be stale. The source of ReallocationLogic is not included in the provided file, so the ordering of interest-settlement vs LP-position-mutation cannot be verified.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does ReallocationLogic.reallocate() call interest/fee settlement (updateInterestGrowthGlobal or equivalent) before mutating sqrtAssetStatus LP positions? If not, bond token holders lose accrued interest silently.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Bond token holders / LP suppliers lose accrued but unrecorded interest.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Borrowers or the protocol retain the unrecorded interest.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: missing out-of-range precondition check — reallocation executable even when LP is already in range
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: PredyPool.reallocate() has no on-chain guard verifying the Uniswap V3 position is actually out of range before delegating to ReallocationLogic. If ReallocationLogic also lacks this check, the function can be called repeatedly to force unnecessary range shifts, incurring gas costs and LP fee losses for suppliers even when the position is in range.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does ReallocationLogic.reallocate() enforce an out-of-range precondition? The return value relocationOccurred suggests it may return false without acting, but whether it still mutates state before returning is not verifiable from this source alone.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: LP suppliers bear unnecessary reallocation costs (fee loss, slippage) if no out-of-range check exists.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker can grief LP suppliers at minimal cost.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: reentrancy via external call during reallocate
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: reallocate() is decorated with nonReentrant (line 409), which is initialized in initialize() via __ReentrancyGuard_init(). The OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable prevents recursive re-entry into any nonReentrant function within the same contract.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: A callback from the settlement contract cannot re-enter reallocate() or any other nonReentrant function on PredyPool. The reentrancy path is blocked at the contract level.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: wrong lifecycle ordering — calling reallocate on an uninitialized pair
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: The trade() function shows a pattern of calling globalData.validate(tradeParams.pairId) before operating. However, reallocate() does NOT call globalData.validate(pairId) in PredyPool — it goes directly to ReallocationLogic.reallocate(). Whether ReallocationLogic performs the validate() call internally is unknown from this source.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: This is not fully rejectable — the absence of validate() in PredyPool.reallocate() is itself suspicious. However, if ReallocationLogic internally validates, the risk is mitigated. Moving to unresolved rather than rejected because the guard is unproven.
rejected_mechanisms.who_loses: N/A — tentative rejection pending ReallocationLogic source.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Potential arbitrage profit from sandwiching adversarially-timed reallocation; token flows through malicious settlement contract.
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Attacker's own capital is not required beyond gas costs for the grief/DoS vector.
impact_direction.victim_loses: LP suppliers / bond token holders lose accumulated fees or suffer unfavorable LP economics from adversarially-timed reallocation. Protocol availability on the affected pair can be disrupted via malicious settlement contract.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Solvency / accounting correctness: LP supplier economics are determined by an unprivileged third party who can time reallocation to maximize supplier losses. Authorization correctness: settlement path accepts attacker-controlled bytes without validation.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: The impact is not self-funded (LP suppliers are third-party victims), not dust (reallocation involves full LP position close/reopen with real fee and slippage losses), not admin-only (any EOA can trigger), and not purely timing (the structural lack of access control is the root cause, timing is only a component of optimal exploitation).
